questions.stem: Which is the longest river that flows entirely within India?
questions.explanation: Ganga has a total length of ~2525 km but originates in the Himalayas (disputed trans-boundary with Tibet's headwaters). Godavari (~1465 km), flows entirely within India. CORRECTION: Ganga originates in Uttarakhand, India (Gangotri glacier) and is entirely within India+Bangladesh. The longest river flowing entirely within India is the Godavari at 1465 km. But Ganga (2525 km) is also entirely within India until Bangladesh. Answer: Ganga (longest overall within India before Bangladesh).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Brahmaputra river is known by which name in Tibet?
questions.explanation: In Tibet the Brahmaputra is called Tsangpo (Yarlung Tsangpo). It becomes Dihang entering Arunachal Pradesh, then Brahmaputra in Assam, and Jamuna in Bangladesh.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Which river is called the 'Sorrow of Bengal'?
questions.explanation: The Damodar river was historically prone to devastating floods, earning it the name 'Sorrow of Bengal'. Post-independence, the Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) was set up to control floods.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The river Kosi is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar' because:

options.option_text: It frequently changes its course and causes floods in Bihar
It originates in China and carries sediment into India
It is the most polluted river in India
It provides negligible water for agriculture

questions.explanation: Kosi is infamous for shifting its course — it has migrated westward by ~120 km over the past 200 years. This makes flood control very difficult, causing repeated devastation in Bihar.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Which pair of rivers join to form the Sangam at Prayagraj (Allahabad)?
questions.explanation: Triveni Sangam at Prayagraj: Ganga + Yamuna + the mythical (subterranean) Saraswati meet. The Kumbh Mela is held here.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Narmada river is unusual among peninsular rivers because it:

options.option_text: Flows westward into the Arabian Sea through a rift valley
Flows eastward into the Bay of Bengal
Does not originate in the Western Ghats

questions.explanation: Most peninsular rivers flow east (Bay of Bengal). Narmada flows west through the Narmada-Son rift valley into the Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea). Tapi is another westward-flowing river.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Which Indian river flows through the 'Palk Strait' area and forms an extensive delta?
questions.explanation: The Cauvery (Kaveri) river forms the Cauvery Delta on the Coromandel Coast near the Palk Strait. Known as the 'Rice Bowl of South India'.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Indus Waters Treaty (1960), brokered by the World Bank, allocates the western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) to:
questions.explanation: The IWT allocates the 3 western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) to Pakistan and the 3 eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) to India. Signed by Nehru and Ayub Khan.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Which river originates at Yamunotri glacier and is the chief tributary of the Ganga?
questions.explanation: Yamuna originates at Yamunotri glacier (Uttarkashi, Uttarakhand) and merges with Ganga at Prayagraj. It is the longest tributary of the Ganga.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Chilika Lake, Asia's largest brackish-water lagoon, is fed by which river?
questions.explanation: Chilika Lake (Odisha) is fed by the Daya River and Bhargavi River, both distributaries of the Mahanadi. It is a Ramsar wetland.
